er_v06_c01_b001_01: Oh, so this is what the lower levels call a 'shop'?
er_v06_c01_b001_02: Incredible. For a bunch of frogs who've never seen the sky, I suppose it'll do.
er_v06_c01_b001_03: Hey. You there. I need food before I can get back to the upper district.
er_v06_c01_b001_04: Food's over there. Prices are on the labels.
er_v06_c01_b001_05: Labels? ...Oh. Right. Everything costs money down here.
er_v06_c01_b001_06: Pick something fresh. And don't try to fob me off with nutrifruit mashed into a different shape and passed off as something else.
er_v06_c01_b002_01: It won't be long before they realise what a stupid mistake they've made.
er_v06_c01_b002_03: They locked up my mother for embezzlement. And she runs the largest hydroponics farm on the entire station!
er_v06_c01_b002_04: Ridiculous. Half the people on this station can eat because of her!
er_v06_c01_b002_05: She triple-checked the accounts just to replace a broken grow light. Embezzlement? Her?
er_v06_c01_b002_07: No. They won't even let me back into the upper district.
er_v06_c01_b002_08: It's fine. This is temporary. Once they sort out their mistake, I won't spend another day down here.
er_v06_c01_b003_01: That's the price? You didn't try to squeeze a little extra out of me?
er_v06_c01_b003_02: The label says what it costs. That's what I charge.
er_v06_c01_b003_03: Hmph. So not everyone in the lower levels is a swindler.
er_v06_c01_b004_03: ...I haven't fallen so low that I need a pawnshop owner to pity me.
er_v06_c01_b004_04: But since you insist, I'll take it. I'll remember this. Don't expect a thank-you.
er_v06_c01_b005_01: That's all? In the upper district this would buy two portions.
er_v06_c01_b005_03: I can see that. The goods are from the lower levels. The prices are upper-district.
er_v06_c01_b006_01: What? You don't even have food? And you call this a shop?
er_v06_c01_b006_03: Unbelievable... Fine. I'll look somewhere else.
er_v06_c01_b007_01: My name is Eleanor. My mother's name will probably be in the news soon.
er_v06_c01_b007_02: A name doesn't change the price.
er_v06_c01_b007_03: I didn't ask you to change it! ...Just remember to save me something fresh next time.
er_v06_c02_b001_01: I can't believe I'm stuck here.
er_v06_c02_b001_02: No word from my mother, and they won't let me go back up. Why is this happening to me?
er_v06_c02_b001_05: Cups, something to clean with... and a lamp that doesn't need two taps before it turns on.
er_v06_c02_b001_06: Looks like I'll be here for a while.
er_v06_c02_b001_07: I found a half-decent room across from the ration station. Small, but at least it doesn't smell.
er_v06_c02_b002_01: This cup has a chip in it.
er_v06_c02_b002_02: That's why it's cheap. The intact ones are over there.
er_v06_c02_b002_03: I was only asking. It's not as if I can't afford an intact one.
er_v06_c02_b002_04: So which one do you want?
er_v06_c02_b002_05: ...The cheap one. The chip isn't on the drinking side.
er_v06_c02_b002_06: My roommate says fix the door lock first, then think about curtains.
er_v06_c02_b002_08: She also says the bottle of perfume I brought would cover half a month's rent.
er_v06_c02_b002_10: You can tell? I thought you only knew scrap metal.
er_v06_c02_b002_11: In this business, you have to know the expensive things too.
er_v06_c02_b003_01: Same price you quoted. Fine, I'll take these.
er_v06_c02_b004_01: Cheaper again? Do you do this for every customer?
er_v06_c02_b004_03: I don't need you fussing over me. ...I'll take the lamp.
er_v06_c02_b005_01: The same goods cost more here than anywhere else?
er_v06_c02_b005_02: This is my first time living in the lower levels. It doesn't mean I can't do arithmetic!
er_v06_c02_b006_01: Forget it. I'll look around. There must be more than one shop down here.
er_v06_c02_b007_01: The neighbours argue every night. It sounds like they're right next to my bed.
er_v06_c02_b007_04: I can't believe people down here live like this their whole lives.
er_v06_c03_b001_02: My funds are running low. They didn't let me bring much with me.
er_v06_c03_b001_03: As soon as I get back up there, I can explain everything and clear our names. Then everything can go back to normal.
er_v06_c03_b001_04: And I'll never have to eat nutrifruit for every meal again.
er_v06_c03_b001_05: Anyway, I brought some of my own things to sell. Water, perfume, a few household items.
er_v06_c03_b001_07: Careful! The cap on that bottle is loose.
er_v06_c03_b001_09: Down here, I don't need to smell like I'm going to a banquet.
er_v06_c03_b001_10: Besides, I doubt I'll be invited to any more banquets.
er_v06_c03_b002_01: *opens the cap and sniffs* Custom blend from an upper-district salon, more than half full. Original bottle. The cap's just loose.
er_v06_c03_b002_03: You don't see bottles like this down here twice a year. See one once and you remember it.
er_v06_c03_b002_04: I thought you'd treat it like ordinary perfume and give me some random price.
er_v06_c03_b002_05: Random prices ruin my own reputation.
er_v06_c03_b002_06: Then keep calculating. You're really going to price every single item?
er_v06_c03_b002_07: Would you rather I price it by your family name?
er_v06_c03_b002_08: Lately, people who price by my name won't offer a single credit.
er_v06_c03_b002_09: No one else in your family can help?
er_v06_c03_b002_10: I don't have any family left. Only my mother.
er_v06_c03_b003_01: Less than I expected. But you explained each item.
er_v06_c03_b004_01: What about the depreciation you mentioned? Did you forget halfway through?
er_v06_c03_b004_02: I have a use for this lot.
er_v06_c03_b004_03: It had better be true. I don't want to come back and see them still sitting here, as if waiting for me to pity them.
er_v06_c03_b005_01: You know what it's worth. You also know I'm short on money.
er_v06_c03_b005_02: ...Fine. Today you caught me at a bad time.
er_v06_c03_b006_01: Fine, I'll take them. If you won't buy, someone else will.
er_v06_c03_b007_01: There's also this. My mother gave it to me.
er_v06_c03_b007_03: ...Ask me for a price first. I haven't decided.
er_v06_c03_b007_04: Then put it away. Take it out when you've decided.
er_v06_c03_b007_05: Aren't you afraid I'll sell it somewhere else?
er_v06_c03_b007_07: ...All right. I'm not selling this one today.
er_v06_c04_b001_01: Hello there. You know Eleanor, don't you? I'm her... uncle.
er_v06_c04_b001_02: We prepared a little gift for her. Only the best from the upper district.
er_v06_c04_b001_03: But I can't find her anywhere.
er_v06_c04_b001_04: An uncle who can't find his own niece?
er_v06_c04_b001_05: Young people get upset and hide. I hear she comes here often.
er_v06_c04_b001_06: Next time she visits, could you give this to her?
er_v06_c04_b001_07: Make sure it reaches her hands. Not yours. Hers.
er_v06_c04_b001_09: I told you. The best the upper district has to offer. She'll understand the moment she sees it.
er_v06_c04_b001_10: If anyone asks, you never saw me.
er_v06_c04_b001_11: Oh, and keep Security out of this. It's a family matter.
er_v06_c04_b002_01: Good. Put it in her hands, not yours. I'll know.
er_v06_c04_b003_01: Hello, shopkeeper. You reported stolen goods?
er_v06_c04_b003_02: I didn't steal it! I have the receipt right here.
er_v06_c04_b003_03: Then why did you report it as stolen?
er_v06_c04_b003_05: Filing a false theft report is a crime. Come along quietly.
er_v06_c04_b003_06: You run a shop, boss. Mind your own counter.
er_v06_c04_b003_07: Someone tampered with my counter. That makes it my business.
er_v06_c04_b004_01: *tells her about the man claiming to be her uncle*
er_v06_c04_b004_02: My uncle? I don't have an uncle.
er_v06_c04_b004_03: I told you. Apart from my mother, I don't have any family left.
er_v06_c04_b005_01: That crate was reported stolen. I called Security. The person who filed the report was him.
er_v06_c04_b005_02: He left me a crate? One that was reported stolen?
er_v06_c04_b005_03: They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
er_v06_c04_b006_01: The crate was reported stolen. It's in my storeroom now. Don't touch it.
er_v06_c04_b006_02: A 'gift' that was reported stolen... They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
er_v06_c04_b007_01: I didn't take it. He couldn't explain where it came from.
er_v06_c04_b007_03: If anyone else claims to be my family, throw him out.
er_v06_c04_b008_01: My mother is already locked up. Isn't that enough for them?
er_v06_c04_b008_02: I... I need some time to think.
er_v06_c04_b008_03: Before all this, if someone sent me a crate like that, I wouldn't even check the label. I'd just open it.
er_v06_c04_b008_05: Now I know nothing in the lower levels comes free. Nothing in the upper district either.
er_v06_c04_b008_06: But you warned me. Please take something. It's the last thing I brought from home.
er_v06_c04_b009_01: I'll come back when I've sorted out my thoughts.
er_v06_c05_b001_02: My money's gone. Last night someone broke in and took what little I had left.
er_v06_c05_b001_03: Only this locket survived because I was wearing it.
er_v06_c05_b001_05: I wasn't there. My roommate went to ask around. I haven't heard from her since.
er_v06_c05_b001_06: The verdict came down too. They found my mother guilty.
er_v06_c05_b001_07: I don't know what to do. I'll be stuck down here forever, and my mother will rot in that cell.
er_v06_c05_b001_08: I kept thinking about how I'd explain to her that I sold everything we brought from home.
er_v06_c05_b001_09: Now... I don't even have the chance to explain.
er_v06_c05_b001_11: I can't believe I've sunk low enough to ask this.
er_v06_c05_b001_12: But could you spare some food? Anything edible. Please.
er_v06_c05_b002_01: Thank you. I won't forget this.
er_v06_c05_b002_02: That's enough. Really. Don't bring out any more.
er_v06_c05_b002_03: Take an extra portion. For your roommate.
er_v06_c05_b002_04: ...She split her own dinner with me yesterday.
er_v06_c05_b002_05: The first day I came here, I called you frogs in a well. I said people down here live like this their whole lives.
er_v06_c05_b002_07: Couldn't you just say you don't remember?
er_v06_c05_b002_08: ...I'm sorry. Those things I said were wrong.
er_v06_c05_b003_01: I don't have any food today either.
er_v06_c05_b003_02: ...I saw the shelves. You don't have to explain.
er_v06_c05_b003_03: If you ever get more stock, could you save me a little? Just a little.
er_v06_c05_b004_01: ...I understand. You run a shop, not a charity.
er_v06_c05_b004_02: When I have money, I'll buy at full price.
er_v06_c05_b005_03: Me begging you for food. And me apologising.
er_v06_c05_b006_01: Don't tell anyone I came here to beg today.
er_v06_c05_b006_03: Thank you. There aren't many things I can still decide for myself. Let me keep this one.
er_v06_c05_b007_01: Don't move! That crate was reported stolen.
er_v06_c05_b007_02: What? It's not mine! I've never seen it before!
er_v06_c05_b007_03: Like mother, like daughter. Come with us.
er_v06_c05_b007_04: Please, someone set me up! Shopkeeper, tell them!
er_v06_c05_b008_01: Did you sort it out with them?
er_v06_c05_b008_03: I said it over and over in there. The crate wasn't mine.
er_v06_c05_b008_04: One of the officers laughed. He said my mother said the same thing.
er_v06_c05_b008_06: Yes. But she's still in there.
er_v06_c05_b009_01: I shouldn't have handed it to you directly.
er_v06_c05_b009_02: You were tricked too. ...But next time, ask me first. All right?
er_v06_c05_b010_01: You knew it was reported stolen?
er_v06_c05_b010_03: Then don't act as if getting me out makes it never happen.
er_v06_c05_b011_01: I'll write down what you spent on me. I'll pay back every credit.
er_v06_c05_b011_04: If I have it, I'll give it to you. If not, we'll think of something together.
